chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) came out of the bathhouse, put on his clothes and wrapped his turban. He said to me: 'When you come out of the bathhouse, wear a turban.' He (the narrator) said: 'So I did not leave off wearing the turban when coming out of the bathhouse, in winter or in summer.'

key_terms.تَعَمَّمَ: Wrapped a turban / wore a turban

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling or recommendation regarding wearing a turban after bathing in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s emphasis on maintaining dignified attire (*takhalluq*) immediately after bathing, ensuring one is covered and presentable before leaving the public space of the bathhouse. The narrator’s lifelong adherence in both seasons underscores the practicality and enduring relevance of this etiquette as a manifestation of inner purity and outward modesty in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> went out from the bathhouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> had worn clothes and a turban. He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Whenever you come out from the bathhouse, so wear a turban’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did not neglect the turban during my coming out from the bathhouse, during the winter and the summer’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabaliy from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Sometimes when on a journey we do not find bran; if we can rub with flour.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful. It is bad only when belongings are destroyed and the body is harmed. If body is benefited then it is not bad. I sometimes command my slave to prepare bleached flour with oil and I rub with it.’”
